Done. Both lessons saved.

Summary of what was generalizable and is now recorded:

1. **Rounding-rule precedence** (skill + memory): an inline per-sub-answer rounding rule ("YoY rate rounded to hundredths") overrides a trailing global rule ("all numbers to thousandths"). My only real format error — I emitted 2.806 instead of 2.81. Different values in one bracket can legitimately have different decimal places.

2. **OLS-on-ln(value) regression + 1-based FY index** (skill + memory): the "fiscal year index" is 1-based (first FY = 1). The slope is origin-invariant but a 0-based index shifts the intercept by exactly one slope-step — which is precisely why my slope was perfect (0.030) but my intercept was off by ~0.03 (8.736 vs 8.706). The diagnostic "intercept_error ≈ slope ⇒ off-by-one index base" is now in the skill, with the numpy.polyfit recipe.

3. **Average YoY over an inclusive FY range** (skill): arithmetic mean of the N-1 consecutive growth ratios ×100 — not a CAGR.

Two of my three values were essentially right; the misses were both convention errors (rounding place, index base) rather than data-extraction errors, so these notes should directly prevent the same near-misses next time.
